title: Progress of area coverage under Kharif crops  as on 07.08.2026

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare released data on Kharif crop sowing progress as on 07.08.2026, showing total area sown at 967.92 lakh hectares, a decrease of 17.96 lakh hectares compared to the same date in 2025 (985.89 lakh hectares). Rice sowing fell the most (down 15.90 lakh ha), followed by coarse cereals (down 4.71 lakh ha, largely due to maize) and pulses (down 1.95 lakh ha), while oilseeds registered a net increase of 5.19 lakh hectares, driven by groundnut, sesamum and sunflower.
enrichment.context: India releases weekly progress reports on Kharif (monsoon-sown) crop area during the sowing season (June-September) to track how planting compares with the five-year normal area and the previous year, serving as an early indicator of agricultural output, food security, and rural income prospects ahead of the harvest. Kharif crops—including rice, pulses, coarse cereals (Shri Anna), oilseeds, sugarcane, jute/mesta and cotton—account for the bulk of India's foodgrain and cash crop production, and lower-than-normal sowing, especially in rice and pulses, can signal delayed or deficient monsoon rainfall in key growing states, with implications for food inflation, MSP procurement planning, and import/export policy for items like edible oils and pulses. The government's push for diversification toward oilseeds and 'Shri Anna' (millets) under initiatives like the National Mission on Edible Oils-Oilseeds and the International Year of Millets legacy programmes also makes crop-wise area trends relevant to policy monitoring, since a rise in oilseed acreage (up 5.19 lakh ha here) aligns with the aim of reducing India's heavy dependence on edible oil imports, while a decline in rice and coarse cereal sowing warrants monitoring for potential production and price impacts.

prelims_questions.question: With reference to the Kharif crop sowing progress report released by the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, which of the following categories showed an INCREASE in area sown as on 07.08.2026 compared to the same date in 2025?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, oilseeds area increased by 5.19 lakh hectares over the corresponding period in 2025, driven mainly by groundnut, sesamum and sunflower, whereas rice, pulses and coarse cereals all registered a decrease.

prelims_questions.question: 'Shri Anna', frequently referenced in India's crop area statistics, refers to which of the following?
options: A category of pulses grown mainly in rainfed areas
Millets and coarse cereals such as jowar, bajra, ragi and small millets
A government scheme for sugarcane farmers
A newly introduced high-yield rice variety
prelims_questions.explanation: 'Shri Anna' is the term used by the Government of India to refer to millets and coarse cereals (jowar, bajra, ragi, small millets, maize), promoted for their nutritional and climate-resilience benefits, especially after the International Year of Millets 2023.
